h: Lakes, Wildlife and a Bit of Putting
p: Rushden Lakes sits right on the edge of the Nene Wetlands, which makes it a cracking spot for a day that mixes indoor fun with the great outdoors. The wetlands are home to all sorts of birdlife, with footpaths along the water's edge and plenty of quiet corners to stop and look out across the lakes. If you've got kids who love spotting ducks, swans and the odd heron, it's a lovely contrast to the neon of the golf course.

A little further afield, Stanwick Lakes is another popular nature spot with walks, cycle routes and play areas, perfect if you fancy more fresh air. Combine either with a round of golf and you've got a day that suits everyone from the toddlers to the grandparents.

On the course, the trick is patience. Take a moment to work out the line of each hole, think about bouncing your ball off the sides, and don't hit it harder than you need to. Gentle putts win far more holes than big whacks. With younger players, agree a maximum number of shots per hole so nobody gets stuck, and be generous with a do-over or two.
After your round, Rushden Lakes has plenty of food options and shops, so you can refuel and carry on exploring without needing to move the car. Easy.
